project.name: libredwg
project.checkout_note: The staged ARVO workspace that reproduced the crash is at a8656c2dc58d2deb857dad8ab0f8ef07ccba52ca. The staged patch/fixed-commit metadata point to an unrelated decode_preR13_entities change for OSS-Fuzz 47189.

classification.classification_note: The saved Stage 01 evidence is an AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1 in json_cquote. The underlying bug is a fixed 46-byte pre-R13 header field being treated as a NUL-terminated C string during JSON escaping.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 54625 (libredwg): Heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1 in json_cquote via json_preR13_header_write_private -> dwg_write_json.
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / exact staged vulnerable source from gt-arvo_54625-workspace:/src/libredwg / patch.diff / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / staged poc bytes / git rev-parse HEAD inside the ARVO workspace container
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run reproduces the crash against the staged ARVO checkout `a8656c2dc58d2deb857dad8ab0f8ef07ccba52ca`, whose source lines match `examples/llvmfuzz.c:130/191`, `header_variables_r11.spec:145`, `json_header_write:1865`, and `dwg_write_json:2389`. The exact 3806-byte witness starts with `AC1001`, so `dwg_decode()` materializes a pre-R13 version, copies it into `dat->from_version`, and because `dwg` starts zeroed in `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()`, the `if (!dwg->header.version)` guard then sets `dat->version` / `dwg->header.version` to that same pre-R13 value. `decode_preR13_header_variables()` later executes `FIELD_TFF (unknown_46, 46, 0)`, copying 46 raw bytes into `dwg->header_vars.unknown_46[46]` without appending a terminator. Before output, `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()` re-materializes the decode-side version state onto the writer `Bit_Chain` with `bit_chain_set_version (&out_dat, &dat)`, so `json_header_write()` also takes the pre-R13 path. There the writer-side `FIELD_TFF` macro expands to `FIELD_TFv`, computes `_l1 = 6 * 46 + 1 = 277`, allocates `_buf`, and calls `json_cquote(_buf, (const char*)_obj->unknown_46, _l1)`. `json_cquote()` stops only on a NUL in the source string, not after 46 bytes, so on this exact witness it scans beyond `unknown_46`, exhausts the 277-byte heap buffer, and then performs the ASan-reported 1-byte heap write inside `json_cquote`. The staged `patch.diff` and metadata `fixed_commit` instead edit `decode_preR13_entities()` for OSS-Fuzz 47189 and do not touch this reproduced `out_json.c` path.

source.description: First project-code statement on the crashing path that interprets attacker bytes into the dispatch state later reused by both decode and JSON output.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` begins with the six bytes `41 43 31 30 30 31` (`AC1001`), so this statement materializes a pre-R13 DWG version.
source.note: This is the earliest project read that makes the witness follow the vulnerable pre-R13 parser and writer path; the later overflow depends on that version state.

sink.description: Function-level sink. After the fixed-field source scan exhausts the 277-byte escape buffer, `json_cquote()` performs its exhausted-buffer terminator write one byte past that heap allocation.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace is exact only to function `json_cquote`. Static source inspection leaves two viable terminator writes on the exhausted buffer: the guarded `*dest = 0` at line 1335 when `dest >= endp`, or the final `*dest = 0` at line 1380 if the loop exits with `dest == endp`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The pre-R13 JSON writer emits the fixed 46-byte `unknown_46` array through `FIELD_TFv`, which allocates `6 * 46 + 1` bytes and then calls `json_cquote` as if that array were a NUL-terminated string.
root_cause.note: The missing obligation is a source-length bound or explicit terminator for fixed-length `TFF` data before string escaping. The staged patch metadata does not address this site.

tainted_value_origin.description: This is where the 46 attacker bytes later misinterpreted as a C string are copied into the fixed `unknown_46[46]` array.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The decode macro expands to `bit_read_fixed (dat, _obj->unknown_46, 46)`, so it copies 46 raw bytes verbatim and does not append `\0`.

parser_admitted.description: Once `dwg_decode()` recognizes the `AC1001` magic and takes the pre-R13 branch, the witness is admitted to the exact parser that materializes `header_vars.unknown_46` and later feeds it back into the pre-R13 JSON writer.

json_writer_selected.description: The saved ASan stack proves the reproduced run took the JSON-output arm after `bit_chain_set_version (&out_dat, &dat)`, so the writer consumes the `out_dat` version state copied from the decode-side `Bit_Chain`.

coarse_trace.summary: The DWG decoder reads the `AC1001` magic, materializes a pre-R13 version, copies it through `dat->from_version` and `dat->version`, and dispatches the witness into `decode_preR13`.

The pre-R13 header parser reads `numheader_vars` as a value greater than 74, bypasses the early return, and copies 46 raw bytes into `dwg->header_vars.unknown_46[46]` via `FIELD_TFF` without appending a terminator.

The fuzz target copies the decoded pre-R13 version into `out_dat` with `bit_chain_set_version`, and the JSON writer combines that writer-side version with the same `numheader_vars > 74` state to reach the `unknown_46` emission site.

The writer allocates a 277-byte escape buffer and passes the fixed `unknown_46` array to `json_cquote` as if it were NUL-terminated text; the unbounded scan exhausts that buffer and the function's exhausted-buffer terminator write performs the ASan-reported 1-byte heap write.

fine_trace.note: Source. The decoder turns the first six attacker bytes into a DWG version enum. The witness starts with `AC1001`, so this yields a pre-R13 version state.

The parsed version is handed off from the DWG header object into the active input `Bit_Chain`. Later version activation and the writer-side handoff both read `dat->from_version`, not `dwg->header.from_version` directly.

The fuzz target zeroes `dwg` before calling `dwg_decode()` (`examples/llvmfuzz.c:75`), so `dwg->header.version` is still 0 and this guard executes. It promotes the pre-R13 `dat->from_version` from step 2 into the active decode version and stored header version used by the later `PRE (R_13b1)` tests.
Because step 3 made the active version pre-R13, `dwg_decode()` routes the witness into `decode_preR13()` instead of the R13+ decoders.

The pre-R13 file header materializes the header-variable count later checked by both decode and JSON emission. The reproduced path proves this value is greater than 74, because both phases reach the `unknown_46` field guarded by that threshold.
The decode-side early return is not taken on this witness, so parsing continues into the 46-byte `unknown_46` field.
Tainted bytes origin. This macro expands to `bit_read_fixed (dat, _obj->unknown_46, 46)`, so 46 raw bytes are copied from the DWG header into the fixed array `unknown_46[46]` with no terminating NUL.

Before output, the fuzz target re-materializes the writer `Bit_Chain` version state from the decode chain. The macro in `src/bits.h:341-345` copies `version` and `from_version`, so `out_dat.version` comes from step 3 and `out_dat.from_version` comes from step 2.

When the saved run later calls `dwg_write_json (&out_dat, &dwg)` from `examples/llvmfuzz.c:191`, `json_header_write()` tests the writer-side `dat->version` copied in step 8. Because that value is still pre-R13, the writer enters `json_preR13_header_write_private()`.
The writer-side copy of the same threshold check is also not taken, so JSON emission reaches the `unknown_46` field instead of stopping at the older header layout.

Root cause. In `src/out_json.c:282-308`, `FIELD_TFF` aliases `FIELD_TFv`, so this len-46 site takes the `len >= 42` branch, computes `_l1 = 6 * 46 + 1 = 277`, allocates that many bytes, and calls `json_cquote(_buf, (const char*)_obj->unknown_46, _l1)`. The fixed array from step 7 is therefore treated as a NUL-terminated string even though decode only copied 46 raw bytes.

The escaper uses only a NUL terminator to stop; the `_l1` argument from step 11 bounds the destination buffer, not the 46-byte source field. On this exact witness no terminating NUL appears before the 277-byte destination budget is exhausted, so the scan runs past `unknown_46` into adjacent decoded bytes and advances `dest` to `endp`.

Sink. Stage 01's saved ASan trace reports `heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1` in `json_cquote`, and the allocation stack shows the exhausted 277-byte heap region came from step 11's `FIELD_TFF (unknown_46, 46, 0)` emission. Once step 12 has advanced `dest` to `endp`, `json_cquote()` performs its exhausted-buffer terminator write one byte past the allocation. The saved evidence does not distinguish whether that write is the guarded `*dest = 0` at line 1335 or the final `*dest = 0` at line 1380, so this sink remains function-level.

crash_location.line: unknown within function (saved ASan trace only symbolized `json_cquote`)

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged `patch.diff` and metadata `fixed_commit` modify `decode_preR13_entities()` for OSS-Fuzz 47189 and do not touch `out_json.c`, `json_cquote`, or the `FIELD_TFF(unknown_46, 46, 0)` emission site exercised by this saved crash.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: The saved ASan trace is function-exact for `json_cquote`; the fine trace therefore anchors the sink to `json_cquote`'s exhausted-buffer terminator write block rather than to a single inner `*dest` line.
cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes. ASan's allocation context is the same `FIELD_TFF (unknown_46, 46, 0)` emission site used as fine-trace step 11.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The fine trace explains the saved stack `json_cquote -> json_preR13_header_write_private -> json_header_write -> dwg_write_json -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`, and it now includes the decode-side `dat->from_version = dwg->header.from_version;` handoff, the guarded `dat->version = dwg->header.version = dat->from_version;` activation, and the later `bit_chain_set_version (&out_dat, &dat)` writer handoff while the exact inner `json_cquote` terminator line remains unsymbolized.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_54625 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed the staged `poc` to `/out/llvmfuzz` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1` in `json_cquote` with stack `json_preR13_header_write_private -> json_header_write -> dwg_write_json`.

format.name: pre-R13 DWG file
format.contract: Exactly the staged 3806-byte DWG witness in `poc` (sha256 `1c5400f8eb2366db7fc59a0ab2ed73a66f531927e066ccedc228244983403235`). The verified trigger semantics are limited to this witness and the saved Stage 01 path: bytes 0..5 are `AC1001`, so `dwg_decode()` takes the pre-R13 branch; the decoded header count is greater than 74, so decode reaches `unknown_46`; `FIELD_TFF` copies 46 raw bytes into `dwg->header_vars.unknown_46[46]`; `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()` then copies the pre-R13 decode version into `out_dat` with `bit_chain_set_version (&out_dat, &dat)` before the saved run reaches `dwg_write_json()`; and that writer passes the fixed array to `json_cquote` through the len-46 `FIELD_TFv` path. The saved crash proves that, for this exact witness, no NUL appears before `json_cquote` exhausts the 277-byte heap buffer allocated for escaping `unknown_46`; it does not establish a broader family of DWG files beyond those same observed properties.
